_strings.@@e1b4560c91aa: Treaty conformity — GA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from GA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the GA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Georgia conforms. The resident return (Form 500) starts from federal adjusted gross income (2025 Form 500, Line 8: "Federal adjusted gross income (From Federal Form 1040)" with the warning "Do not use FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME"), and adjustments are made only on Form 500 Schedule 1. The Schedule 1 ADDITIONS do not include any add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA add-back). To the contrary, the IT-511 booklet expressly lists as a SUBTRACTION item income specifically exempted by Federal law or treaty. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and GA neither adds it back nor otherwise re-taxes it (and explicitly recognizes the treaty exemption), it flows through untaxed.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 500, Line 16: 'Tax (Multiply Line 15c by 5.19%. Round to the nearest dollar)'. Line 15c Georgia Taxable Income = Line 10 Georgia AGI minus Line 11 standard deduction (or Line 12c itemized), minus Line 14 dependent exemption (Line 7c x $4,000), minus Line 15b Georgia NOL utilized. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 STRUCTURAL CHANGE — HB 111 ACCELERATED THE FLAT RATE: for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 the Georgia flat rate DROPS to 5.19% (2024: 5.39%), per the 2025 IT-511 What's New ('Effective January 1, 2025, the income tax rate is 5.19%') and Form 500 Line 16. The $12,000/$24,000 standard deductions and the $4,000 dependent exemption are UNCHANGED from 2024; personal exemptions remain repealed (only the dependent exemption survives). Do NOT carry the 2024 5.39% rate into 2025, and do NOT use this pack for 2024. Base guidance: Supply Form 500, Line 10 'Georgia adjusted gross income' (Line 8 federal AGI from Form 1040, net of Line 9 adjustments from Form 500 Schedule 1) for a FULL-YEAR resident. The op subtracts the per-status Line 11 standard deduction and $4,000 per dependent (Line 14) to reach Line 15c Georgia taxable income (assuming no Line 15b NOL), then multiplies by 5.19%. Pass exemptions_count=0 — Georgia has NO personal exemption (repealed); pass dependents_count = Form 500 Line 7c (qualified dependents plus unborn dependents). Do not use this op if you itemize deductions, claim a Georgia NOL (Line 15b), or file as a part-year resident/nonresident (they omit Lines 9-14 and use Schedule 3, which prorates the deduction) — compute those on the form. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE (CRITICAL): Georgia files QSS under filing status D 'Head of Household or Qualifying Surviving Spouse' with a $12,000 standard deduction (both the 2025 Form 500 Line 5 status list and the IT-511 Standard Deductions chart, which prints 'Qualifying surviving spouse $12,000') — pass head_of_household to this op, NOT married_filing_jointly. The engine's default QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping would apply MFJ's $24,000 and UNDERSTATE tax. AGE-65/BLIND ADDITIONAL DEDUCTION: none for Georgia — the flat $12,000/$24,000 amounts are the entire standard deduction; the old (pre-2024) $1,300-per-checkbox additional standard deduction is gone. No age_65/blind keys ship. ITEMIZERS NOT MODELED: if you itemized on your federal return (or are MFS and your spouse itemizes), you MUST itemize on the Georgia return (Line 12c = federal Schedule A total less Georgia adjustments) and the standard deduction does not apply. Itemizing residents may claim the Georgia Eligible Itemizer Tax Credit of up to $300 per taxpayer on Form 500 Line 19 — a CREDIT against Line 16 tax, not a base reduction, and not modeled. NO tax table and NO rate schedule: Line 16 is a straight multiplication printed on the form ('Multiply Line 15c by 5.19%. Round to the nearest dollar'). Georgia NOL not modeled: Form 500 Line 15b (Georgia NOL utilized, limited to 80% of Line 15a income for losses from tax years 2018+) is subtracted before Line 15c taxable income. Part-year residents and nonresidents not modeled: they omit Form 500 Lines 9-14 and use Schedule 3, which prorates the standard deduction and dependent exemption by the Georgia-income ratio. This pack's subtractions apply only to full-year residents. Taxpayers required to file federal Form 1040NR generally may NOT take the Georgia standard deduction. NOTE: Form 500-EZ is DISCONTINUED for 2025 — all filers use Form 500. CREDITS (subtracted from tax, NOT modeled and NOT base reductions): Low Income Credit (Form 500 Line 17 — a per-exemption CREDIT of $5-$26 for federal AGI under $20,000); Other State(s) Tax Credit (Line 18); Georgia Eligible Itemizer Tax Credit (Line 19, up to $300 per itemizing taxpayer); IND-CR series 200 credits (Line 20); Schedule 2 series 100 credits (Line 21). Total credits used (Line 22) cannot exceed Line 16 tax. Rounding: the Form 500 Line 16 instruction itself mandates 'Round to the nearest dollar'; this pack rounds half-up to whole dollars (irs_round), matching the form's presentation.
